steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Add the imports for Component decorator and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Component and CommonModule from the same package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing Angular core features
import { Component, NgModule } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component decorator and CommonModule are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Component and CommonModule are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core Angular features needed for component creation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent with basic structure
steps.instruction: Define the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the imported Component decorator and define a class named AppComponent with a selector and template.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component } from '@angular/core';

// Define your AppComponent here
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with a Component decorator and empty template.
successCriteria: AppComponent class is exported with @Component decorator containing selector and empty template string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the root AppComponent structure correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the AppComponent class is exported and has the @Component decorator with selector and template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent structure is incomplete. Check that you've defined the class with the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Create a child HeaderComponent
steps.instruction: Define a new child component named HeaderComponent with its own template containing a header element.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component. Add a selector and template property. The template should contain a <header> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A HeaderComponent class is created with a basic template containing a header element.
successCriteria: HeaderComponent is defined with @Component decorator, has a selector property, and a template containing a <header> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the HeaderComponent with its own template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the HeaderComponent, but make sure it has the @Component decorator with selector and template properties containing a <header> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HeaderComponent isn't properly defined. Check that you used @Component decorator with selector and template containing a <header> element.

steps.title: Add HeaderComponent to AppComponent template
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add the HeaderComponent selector <app-header> to embed the child component.
steps.hint: Place the selector inside the component's template property. The selector is the tag name you defined in HeaderComponent.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template now includes the HeaderComponent selector, enabling component composition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully embedded the HeaderComponent in the AppComponent template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added the <app-header> selector inside the AppComponent template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HeaderComponent selector is not present in the AppComponent template. Add <app-header> inside the template.

steps.title: Create a ContentComponent with input property
steps.instruction: Create a new component named ContentComponent below HeaderComponent. Add an @Input decorator to define a message property of type string.
steps.hint:
Use the @Component decorator with selector 'app-content' and a simple template like

{{message}}

. Don't forget to export the class.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new ContentComponent is defined with an input property that can receive data from a parent component.
successCriteria: ContentComponent is created with selector 'app-content', template containing {{message}}, and @Input() message: string property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a component with an input property, enabling parent-to-child data flow.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the component, but check: does it have the @Input decorator on a message property of type string?
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't fully correct. Ensure you define ContentComponent with @Component, selector 'app-content', template showing {{message}}, and @Input() message: string.

steps.title: Add ContentComponent to AppComponent with data binding
steps.instruction: Add the ContentComponent selector to the AppComponent template and bind a message property to it.
steps.hint: Use the component selector as a custom HTML element and bind a property using square brackets.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template will include the ContentComponent with a bound message property.
successCriteria: ContentComponent selector is added to AppComponent template
Message property is bound using square bracket syntax
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the ContentComponent to the AppComponent template with data binding.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the ContentComponent, but make sure to bind a message property using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ContentComponent isn't properly added or the data binding is missing. Check the selector and binding syntax.

steps.title: Create a ButtonComponent with output event
steps.instruction: Create a new component named ButtonComponent below the existing ContentComponent. Use the @Component decorator with selector 'app-button' and a template containing a button element with the text 'Click me'. Add an @Output decorator named buttonClick that emits an EventEmitter.
steps.hint: Remember to import Output and EventEmitter from '@angular/core' and define the component class with the output property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new ButtonComponent is defined with an output event emitter that will allow child-to-parent communication when the button is clicked.
successCriteria: ButtonComponent is created with selector 'app-button', a button element in the template, and an @Output property named buttonClick of type EventEmitter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ButtonComponent with an output event. This enables the component to communicate with its parent when the button is clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined the ButtonComponent with the correct selector, template, and an @Output property named buttonClick.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ButtonComponent isn't properly defined. Check that you've created the component class with @Component decorator, added a button in the template, and declared an @Output property.

steps.title: Add ButtonComponent to AppComponent with event binding
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add the ButtonComponent selector and bind its buttonClick output to a new handleClick method.
steps.hint: Use the selector 'app-button' and bind the event with (buttonClick)="handleClick()".
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template will include the ButtonComponent with proper event binding.
successCriteria: ButtonComponent selector is added to the template with (buttonClick) event binding to a handleClick method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the ButtonComponent with event binding to the AppComponent template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the ButtonComponent, but the event binding might be incomplete. Check that you used (buttonClick)="handleClick()".
steps.feedbackWrong: The ButtonComponent is not properly added with event binding. Make sure to use the selector 'app-button' and bind the buttonClick output.

steps.title: Define event handler in AppComponent
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent class, create a method named handleButtonClick that logs a message to the console when called.
steps.hint: Add a method inside the AppComponent class that takes no parameters and uses console.log to output a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class now has a handleButtonClick method that logs a message when invoked.
successCriteria: AppComponent contains a method named handleButtonClick that logs a message to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the event handler method in AppComponent. This method will be triggered when the button emits its event.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the method is named exactly handleButtonClick and includes console.log with a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent class should have a method named handleButtonClick that logs a message. Check the method name and the console.log statement.

steps.title: Complete the component composition structure
steps.instruction: Add the ButtonComponent to the AppComponent template with event binding to the handleButtonClick method, and ensure all components are properly defined.
steps.hint: In the AppComponent template, add the <app-button> element with an event binding for (buttonClick). In the AppComponent class, implement the handleButtonClick method. Also, make sure the ContentComponent and ButtonComponent are fully defined with their respective decorators and properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template includes the ButtonComponent with event binding, the handleButtonClick method is implemented, and all child components are properly defined with their input/output properties.
successCriteria: ButtonComponent is added to AppComponent template with (buttonClick) event binding, handleButtonClick method is defined in AppComponent, ContentComponent has @Input message property, and ButtonComponent has @Output buttonClick event emitter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully completed the component composition. All components are properly wired together with input properties and output events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're almost there. Make sure all components are defined with their correct decorators and properties, and the event binding is properly set up.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component composition isn't complete. Check that all components are defined, the ButtonComponent is included in the template with event binding, and the handleButtonClick method is implemented.
